author: WP05
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on the shared GraphicsDevice contract: construction and windows, public state, viewport/scissor, Clear/Present/Reset, the manager event model, render-target and vertex bindings, draws, readback, resources, adapters and extensions. Many claims are stale at TARGET: construction and disposal are now transactional, Clear throws for missing planes, Present and Vector4 Clear overloads exist, redundant target binding is a no-op, readback is HiDef-only and generic, adapters use the platform layer. The Development pages already carried construction, render-target binding and draw validation; two new deep dives now hold the rest.

concepts.text: GraphicsDevice is the public hub of the graphics module: it owns the selected renderer (and a window when the family needs one), stores public pipeline state, tracks resources for ordered teardown, normalises render-target and vertex bindings and forwards draws through IGraphicsRenderer.

Public device state can be valid and readable while a family ignores or approximates the native operation behind it; a property round trip proves only the shared layer, a family is proven only by a test that engages it and checks output.
tokens: A property that round-trips proves only the shared layer

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp (setters store after renderer calls; renderer overrides vary)

concepts.text: Evidence gradient for the call path: a public call reaching IGraphicsRenderer is weaker evidence than visible family engagement, which is weaker than a correct native result (pixel).
Resource classes, renderer defaults and renderer divergences are owned by other subjects; the device page owns only the shared device contract and links to the family and resource pages.
The XNA-shaped constructor takes GraphicsAdapter&, GraphicsProfile and const PresentationParameters&; copy and move of GraphicsDevice are deleted.
The CNAEXT default constructor delegates with the default adapter, GraphicsProfile::Reach and a default PresentationParameters (800 x 480 Color back buffer, no depth, DiscardContents).
concepts.note: The default back-buffer size (800 x 480) was not stated; added.

concepts.text: Which families construct without a window: at TARGET the family descriptor decides (needsWindow false for SOFTWARE, PORTABLEGL, HEADLESS, STUB), and SOFTWARE on a surface-presenter-only platform (terminal on a TTY) receives the terminal as its window.
concepts.note: Compile-time family check replaced by the runtime descriptor; terminal presenter exception added.

concepts.text: PresentationParameters.HeadlessEXT requests a windowless device from a family that normally wants a window; only DIRECTX12 and SDL_GPU honour it, other families (Direct3D 11 swap chain, EasyGL context) throw from their constructor.
concepts.note: Bible named only D3D12; TARGET documents D3D12 and SDL_GPU.

concepts.text: A windowed default device gets a platform window sized from the back buffer (800 x 480 by default; 1024 x 768 only when a dimension is not positive), titled with the default title and not resizable, matching XNA AllowUserResizing == false.
concepts.note: Bible: SDL window usually 1024 x 768. TARGET: platform window (SDL3 by default, also X11/Wayland/Win32), 1024 x 768 is only the fallback.

concepts.text: Game holds the GraphicsDevice as a value member constructed before derived game code; GraphicsDeviceManager reconfigures that same device through Reset and ordinary game code never constructs a second device.

Construction order: capture the caller GL binding, publish TouchPanel size, resolveRenderer (per candidate: video reference, window create/adopt, apply presentation parameters, create renderer), UpdateViewportFromWindow, push default states, restore GL binding. The Bible's SDL-video-first order predates the platform layer.
concepts.note: Platform-neutral order replaces SDL_InitSubSystem; development page already had the full sequence, the deep dive restates it with the window rules.

concepts.text: Both CNA-created and caller-attached windows are published to Mouse and TextInputEXT so input targets the device window.

After the renderer exists the constructor pushes BlendState::Opaque, DepthStencilState::Default (skipped when SupportsDepthStencil is false) and RasterizerState::CullCounterClockwise to the real renderer, as FNA does.

An attached DeviceWindowHandle is borrowed: at TARGET the platform wrapper from AdoptWindowHandle cannot destroy it and ownsWindow_ is only the fallback policy "may CNA rebuild this window"; input handles pointing at it are cleared at teardown.
concepts.note: Ownership moved from an SDL pointer flag to the platform wrapper.

concepts.text: Limitation claimed: construction was not transactional; a later window, renderer or initial-state exception could leak the owned window, the published input handle or the video-subsystem lease.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the constructor catches every exception from resolveRenderer/UpdateViewportFromWindow/state push, destroys native resources, releases the video reference and rethrows; page states it as current behaviour with a one-line historical note.

concepts.text: Limitation claimed: teardown called SDL_QuitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_VIDEO) even for a device that never initialised video, releasing another client's reference.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the video reference is a bool changed only by setVideoSubsystemAcquired, released only when held; comment records the merge defect that was fixed.

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp (setVideoSubsystemAcquired: single Boolean reference, release only if acquired)

concepts.text: Evidence caveat: tests covered windowless operation but not injected construction failure; at TARGET CNA_DEBUG_FAIL_RENDERER_INIT injects a renderer initialisation failure and the fallback tests use it.
concepts.note: Mixed-client video reference accounting is still not tested.

concepts.text: The device property surface grouped by ownership: identity and lifecycle, display, shader slots, pipeline state and bindings, each with its own storage and forwarding contract.

Claim that only D3D9 drives the lost/not-reset status callback: at TARGET six families call deviceEventCallback (DIRECTX9, DIRECTX11, DIRECTX12, DIRECT2D, WEBGPU report loss and reset; VULKAN reports Lost once).
concepts.note: Header comments still say D3D9 only; noted on the page.

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp (createRenderer deviceEventCallback); grep of modules/renderers for deviceEventCallback

concepts.text: Viewport and scissor are stored and forwarded; the getter returns the stored logical value and is not a native-state query.

Device texture collections are not a general shader binding mechanism: stock effects carry their own texture through FillGpuDrawParams, ShaderEffect uses its own setters, and only compiled XNA effects read (and publish into) the device Textures/SamplerStates collections; sampler state is pushed before every draw.
concepts.note: Compiled effects now read the collections; the Bible said textures never reach a draw through them.

concepts.text: State objects assigned to the device are bound (immutable afterwards) and share their payload; reassigning the active object is a no-op; setters validate profile rules and commit only after the renderer accepted the state. The Bible's "copied, reassign after mutation" advice is wrong at TARGET.
concepts.note: Mutation after binding throws InvalidOperationException.

concepts.text: Singular and plural vertex-buffer setters share one coherent binding state (the list), so the two getters agree.
Assigning Textures[0] does not make a BasicEffect draw sample that texture; the stock effect samples its own Texture property.

TextureCollection enforces slot range, disposed textures and active-render-target refusal, and for the vertex stage the profile slot count (4 under HiDef, none under Reach); the setter is spelled textures(slot, texture).
concepts.note: Profile slot counts added.

concepts.text: Viewport and scissor setters validate first (ArgumentException, state unchanged, rectangle must fit the active surface, depth range 0..1 ordered), map logical to presentation rectangle, call the renderer and store only after it returned.
concepts.note: Validation and logical mapping added to the Bible's apply-then-retain order.

concepts.text: Scissor enable is RasterizerState::ScissorTestEnable, separate from the rectangle; a scissor test must draw across the boundary because a property round trip proves only storage.

Construction installs the full logical viewport; UpdateViewportFromWindow resets viewport and scissor only when the logical size or physical default rectangle changed compared with its own last record.
Present() preserves custom viewport and scissor while the logical size and physical rectangle are unchanged.

Render-target transitions reset viewport and scissor to the first target (or back buffer), but an unchanged binding set returns early, so a redundant rebinding keeps the game's rectangles (Bible said every switch resets, even redundant ones).
A family may use a physical default viewport distinct from the logical public size (letterbox/overscan) through GetDefaultViewportRect.

Clear(Color) uses XNA default clear options (target plus the depth/stencil planes that really exist), depth 1.0f independent of Viewport.MaxDepth, stencil 0 (Bible: all three aspects with Viewport.MaxDepth).
Clear(ClearOptions, Color, depth, stencil) is the central overload that clears exactly the requested aspects.
Clear(r, g, b, a) is a CNAEXT direct colour clear through the renderer colour hook, without aspect routing.
Clear(Color, depth) is a CNAEXT convenience for Target | DepthBuffer with the given depth.
Claim that FNA's Vector4-colour Clear overload is absent: at TARGET Clear(ClearOptions, Vector4, float, int) exists and quantises through Color like Microsoft XNA.

Claim that CNA has only parameterless Present(): Present(sourceRectangle, destinationRectangle, overrideWindowHandle) exists; empty arguments equal Present(), rectangles are clipped, unsupported requests throw NotSupportedException; only HEADLESS and SOFTWARE implement the region hook.
Present refuses with InvalidOperationException while a user render target is bound (also after a bound target was destroyed).
tokens: Cannot present while render targets are bound

concepts.text: Present calls the renderer and then refreshes viewport/scissor only if the reported destination geometry changed.
ClearOptions is a bitwise combination of Target, DepthBuffer and Stencil; unknown bits are ignored.
Claim that shared code validates the requested depth value: at TARGET depth is normalised as Direct3D does (NaN to 0, clamp to [0, 1]) rather than rejected.
The clear asks independently whether the active 2D/cube target or back buffer has a real depth plane and a real stencil plane.

Claim that absent aspects are masked and a depth/stencil-only clear becomes a no-op matching FNA: at TARGET requesting a missing depth or stencil plane throws InvalidOperationException before anything is cleared (Microsoft XNA behaviour).
tokens: does not have an active depth or stencil buffer
concepts.note: A warning callout explains that Clear(Color, depth) on a depthless target now throws.

concepts.text: A non-empty request is dispatched to exactly one of seven renderer clear methods.
The independent depth/stencil query matters for Depth16/Depth24 versus Depth24Stencil8 and for families with a standalone stencil plane.

Family-specific clear ordering and remaining defects (an EasyGL colour-hook/depth coupling, a D3D9 back-buffer-format gate) were not re-read; the page states only that native ordering is renderer-specific.
concepts.note: Recorded as issue candidate WP05-i011; not published.

target.evidence: not read at TARGET for this page

concepts.text: All four public Reset overloads end in Reset(parameters, adapter*).
Reset raises DeviceResetting first, so handlers still see the old adapter and parameters.
Reset clones the request, normalises applied colour/depth formats, stores adapter and virtual size and updates TouchPanel dimensions; at TARGET it first unbinds every render target (not restored).
concepts.note: Render-target unbinding added at TARGET.

concepts.text: Window state and virtual resolution are applied inside a rollback guard; a failure restores presentation parameters, adapter, virtual size and touch dimensions, tries to restore the window and rethrows the original exception.
After the guard Reset calls UpdatePresentationFormatEXT, ApplyMultiSampleCount (writing the applied count back) and SetSwapInterval, in that order.
concepts.note: Order at TARGET: formats, then MSAA, then interval.

concepts.text: Reset finally refreshes viewport/scissor and raises DeviceReset.

The rollback guard ends before the format, MSAA and interval hooks; a later exception leaves the new parameters stored, targets unbound and DeviceReset unraised, so paired Resetting/Reset handlers must tolerate a missing second half.
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP05-i005.

concepts.text: A successful reset proves the shared route ran, not that a compositor accepted fullscreen or an interval; applied values are stronger than requests but depend on each family's truthful reporting.
tokens: proves that the shared route ran

concepts.text: FNA stores the new state before its resetting event and performs one FNA3D back-buffer reset, so event observations and native transaction shape differ from CNA.
concepts.note: Only the single-reset shape is supported by a CNA comment; the event-order claim is not repeated.

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp (Reset comment on the FNA3D reset order); FNA source not part of TARGET

concepts.text: A game-attached GraphicsDeviceManager registers IGraphicsDeviceManager and IGraphicsDeviceService but does not own the Game device.

CreateDevice raises PreparingDeviceSettings, resets the existing device, subscribes to later device reset events and then raises DeviceCreated; the initial settle-in reset is not forwarded as a manager reset pair.
Later ApplyChanges reaches GraphicsDevice::Reset and the manager forwards the device events exactly once.
Edits made in PreparingDeviceSettings apply to that candidate only and are never copied back into the preferred fields.
The PreparingDeviceSettings callback must keep a non-null adapter: the apply step dereferences it for Reset(parameters, adapter&).
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP05-i003.

concepts.text: The callback must not re-enter ApplyChanges: the preferences-changed flag is cleared only at the end of the pass, so a nested call recurses.
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP05-i004.

concepts.text: Listener exceptions propagate through the manager pipeline and can interrupt the staged operation before or after the reset.

The manager subscribes a lambda capturing raw this to GameWindow::ClientSizeChanged, discards the removal token and removes only services on disposal, so destroying or replacing a manager while the window lives can leave a dangling resize callback.
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP05-i001.

concepts.text: Manager disposal raises DeviceDisposing although it does not delete the Game-owned device; Game subscribes UnloadContent to that event.
The manager raises Disposed before setting its disposed flag, so a re-entrant or throwing Disposed listener is a lifecycle hole.
tokens: before its disposed flag is set
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP05-i002.

concepts.text: SetRenderTarget(RenderTarget2D*), the cube-face overload and SetRenderTargets all funnel into the plural path; an empty list restores the back buffer.
GetRenderTargets() returns a new vector on every call; there is no allocation-free variant.
Each public binding becomes a RenderTargetBindingDescriptor naming a 2D target or cube face, its dimensions and the renderer-applied sample count.
At most four bindings; the one-target Reach limit is not D3D9-only at TARGET but the renderer contract default GetMaxRenderTargetsForProfileEXT on every renderer.
Bindings must be non-null, non-disposed, created by this device and backed by a renderer object (NotSupportedException otherwise).
concepts.note: Foreign-device refusal added.

concepts.text: Cube faces are range-checked and a RenderTarget2D array slice must be 0.
Targets must match in dimensions and applied sample counts, and at TARGET also in pixel size (formats of equal size are compatible).
Claim that distinct faces of one cube may be bound together: XNA compares resource identity, so at TARGET one resource in two slots, including two faces of one cube, is rejected.
tokens: Reject a resource bound to two slots

concepts.text: The native bind must succeed before public bindings, flags and viewport/scissor are committed.

Claim that there is no redundant-binding early return: at TARGET an unchanged binding set returns immediately without resolving, discarding or resetting rectangles (except after a bound target was destroyed).
PreserveContents and PlatformContents retain content; DiscardContents clears colour to opaque black plus each real depth/stencil plane on a real bind.
The API does not guarantee that discarded content later reads as black; portable code must not rely on it.
tokens: should not rely on reading black

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp (discard clear is a CNA implementation choice; XNA semantics undefined)

concepts.text: The render-to-texture sequence: bind target, clear, draw, unbind, verify, then sample the target with SpriteBatch; on a depthless target clear with Clear(Color).

Back-buffer readback while a target is bound was renderer-specific (active target, back buffer, synthetic Headless, refusal); at TARGET the shared layer refuses while a target is bound, and HEADLESS and STUB throw instead of synthesising.
Portable verification of an off-screen result uses RenderTarget2D::GetData after unbinding.

Historical SOFTWARE defect: the sampler cast only to its texture renderer, so a render target sampled as a null texture (white inset); fixed, and Software_RenderTargetReadback checks exact readback plus SpriteBatch and textured-primitive sampling.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the registered test states both pre-fix causes and checks sampling through SpriteBatch; the page keeps it as a labelled historical case.

concepts.text: A producer-side (numeric) check and a consumer-side pixel check answer different questions; both are needed for render-to-texture evidence.
Binding up to four RenderTargetBindings does not establish that one draw writes all attachments; stock effects write attachment 0 only.

target.evidence: docs/render-targets.html#mrt (Phase-1, TARGET-checked); stock effect shaders write one output

concepts.text: Claim that WebGPU rejects MRT: WEBGPU reports MultipleRenderTargets and binds up to the profile limit at TARGET.

Per-family MRT qualifications (Software stock-effect route, D3D12 stock draws writing slot zero, diagnostic renderers recording only logical state) were not re-verified per family; the stock-effect rule covers the stock cases.

target.evidence: not re-read per family for this page

concepts.text: MRT verification method: MultipleRenderTargets is only an initial query; require a successful bind and a shader plus pixel check that distinguishes every output.
SetVertexBuffer(buffer, offset) rejects a negative offset, disposed or foreign buffer and replaces the list with slot 0; null clears the list.
concepts.note: Foreign-device refusal added.

concepts.text: Claim that SetVertexBuffers retains legal null slots: at TARGET it accepts at most 16 bindings, refuses null entries (Microsoft XNA, not FNA) and keeps the processed prefix when a later entry fails.
GetVertexBuffer and GetVertexBuffers agree because both read one list; this corrects an older split-state description.
The Indices property, SetIndexBuffer/GetIndexBuffer and Indices() are three spellings for one index pointer, not independent state.

Buffer-backed draws (DrawPrimitives, DrawIndexedPrimitives, DrawInstancedPrimitives, plus base-instance and indirect EXT forms) run shared validation of arguments, profile ceiling, effect, buffers and ranges before native submission.
concepts.note: Profile ceilings (65,535 / 1,048,575) and EXT routes added.

concepts.text: Sampler state is applied before each draw route.
Generic XNA user-primitive methods become overload sets for raw bytes and the four built-in vertex types, plus std::vector<TVertex> templates.
concepts.note: Vector templates added.

concepts.text: Indexed user draws accept 16- and 32-bit indices; under Reach 32-bit user indices throw NotSupportedException.
Raw layouts need an explicit VertexDeclaration, except that the declaration-less const void* DrawUserPrimitives reads its array as VertexPositionColor objects.
Typed vertex objects are packed into the asserted stream layout because CNA vertex structures are polymorphic (vtable pointer); callers must never reinterpret them as GPU bytes.
User draws pack into device scratch vectors whose capacity persists: a warm-up cost, not an allocation-free promise (each call also creates a temporary renderer vertex buffer).

One helper, FillVertexStreamBindings, serves ordinary and instanced draws and copies up to 16 slot-aligned stream descriptions (buffer, declaration, stride, offset, frequency, capacity, shader-read flag) into GpuDrawParams.
Instanced validation applies baseVertex only to per-vertex streams and requires 1 + floor((first + n - 1) / f) records per read instance stream; the instanced route folds no offset.
concepts.note: Formula generalised for the base-instance EXT route.

concepts.text: Families differ in accepted layouts and native divisor support; a two-stream call that compiles is not a portable arbitrary-effect claim.
Every shared draw starts world/view/projection at identity and asks the applied effect for IEffectMatrices via dynamic_cast.
Stock effects, ShaderEffect, PbrEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect implement IEffectMatrices.

target.evidence: headers deriving from IEffectMatrices (BasicEffect, ShaderEffect, PbrEffect, SkinnedPbrEffect, ...)

concepts.text: A custom effect without IEffectMatrices receives identity transforms rather than an exception, a legitimate route for clip-space vertices.
The CNAEXT static PrimitiveVerts converts a primitive count to the consumed element count, 64-bit checked, throwing for an unknown topology; it mirrors an internal FNA helper.

Claim that GetBackBufferData writes only Color: at TARGET three Color overloads plus three templates for any trivially copyable element type exist, and the method is HiDef-only (NotSupportedException under Reach).
The whole-image size comes from PresentationParameters, a rectangle must be positive and inside the back buffer, and each Color is constructed from RGBA bytes because Color carries a vtable pointer.
tokens: first byte is not the red channel

concepts.text: Former caller-safety gaps (negative startIndex unchecked, elementCount >= pixel count, unchecked width x height overflow) are closed: startIndex must be non-negative, sizes are 64-bit checked and elementCount must cover exactly the requested bytes.
concepts.note: Positive evidence in the validation block; the remaining caller duty (destination capacity) is the next concept.

concepts.text: C++ cannot see the destination length, so the caller must still provide startIndex + elementCount elements.
The method name does not define one image across families; pixel evidence must name the family and the coordinate space.

target.evidence: renderer ReadBackbuffer implementations differ (Vulkan submit, Headless/Stub throw)

concepts.text: The device keeps a non-owning vector of resource addresses; the base resource constructor registers this and raises ResourceCreated before the derived renderer object exists.
Derived disposal releases the renderer object; the base raises the device ResourceDestroyed, unregisters and marks itself disposed.
Destructor-driven Dispose(false) suppresses the resource Disposing event but still raises the device ResourceDestroyed while the device lifetime token is alive.

Claim of device disposal order (resources, Disposing, native teardown, video quit, disposed flag last): at TARGET the flag is set first, Disposing is raised (explicit only) before resources are disposed, then native teardown and video release.
Limitation claimed: a still-bound RenderTarget2D could throw during device disposal after the registry was cleared, preventing renderer teardown.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the bound-target refusal is skipped once the device is disposed, and the device marks itself disposed first.

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/RenderTarget2D.cpp (Dispose: guard only while device not disposed); GraphicsDeviceLifecycleTest.DisposalIsReentrantAndReleasesABoundRenderTarget

concepts.text: Limitation claimed: a device Disposing listener could re-enter because IsDisposed stayed false until after teardown.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: flag set before callbacks and a test pins it.

concepts.text: Advice to unbind targets before explicit device disposal is no longer needed for correctness; outside device teardown disposing a bound target still throws and destruction while bound leaves Present refusing.
Renderer-specific in-flight and deferred destruction rules belong to the family pages (Vulkan retirement by frame generation).

Claim that GraphicsResource copy/move never repair the registry: moves transfer the registry entry and device bindings; Texture2D copies share the renderer object and add no registry entry; value states share one identity.
Keep live resources within the device lifetime and do not rely on a copy being tracked or disposed by the device.
tokens: keep live resources inside the device's lifetime

concepts.text: GraphicsAdapter exposes display modes, Description (display name), synthetic DeviceName, MonitorHandle (display id), default and widescreen flags and identity fields; IsWideScreen uses XNA's > 1.6 rule.
concepts.note: Widescreen rule and display-id handle added.

concepts.text: VendorId and DeviceId are best-effort reads from /sys/class/drm/card0..3 on Linux and 0 elsewhere.
Revision and SubSystemId are always 0.
DisplayMode holds width, height, format and computed aspect ratio (and a title-safe area).

Claim that the three device exception types are thin runtime_error subclasses: at TARGET DeviceLostException, DeviceNotResetException and NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException derive from System::Exception.

Adapters are built lazily, one per display reported by the platform display service (not SDL directly), cached as unique_ptr; with no display a single synthetic 800 x 480 "Default Display" adapter is used.
AdaptersChanged destroys and rebuilds the cache; references held across it dangle and DefaultAdapter must be re-read.
DefaultAdapter is the current first entry, not a separate GPU-selection service; the renderer decides the GPU.
DIRECTX9 is the only family whose IsProfileSupported consults native device capabilities; every other build returns true for both profiles.

Claim that only D3D9 consults the device for render-target/back-buffer queries and others use a shared list with zero samples: at TARGET the profile rule applies everywhere, D3D9/D3D11/D3D12 and the GLES/WebGL EasyGL identities supply format hooks, and D3D9/D3D11/D3D12/Vulkan clamp sample counts.
These adapter methods are not portable hardware probes; after device creation prefer device-level answers.
Resource instrumentation extensions (create/destroy hooks, add/remove reference, tracked count) are public for framework plumbing and tests.
Claim that renderer identity is compile-time: GetGraphicsRendererType reports this device's actual, runtime-selected renderer.
Claim that SupportsCapability is optimistic unless the family overrides: at TARGET six of the 19 members are derived at device level and MultipleRenderTargets is ANDed with the profile limit.
GetMaxTextureDimension reports the renderer limit, enforced by the texture and content paths.
The unsupported-3D call policy is a device extension (Get/SetUnsupported3DGraphicsCallBehavior).

State and effect plumbing (depth/blend/write toggles, SetCurrentEffect, SetGraphicsProfileEXT, SetPresentationParameters) are internal routes, not substitutes for XNA state objects or a runtime profile switch; the toggles bypass the public state objects.
Debug/recovery members (context recovery, string marker, GetRenderer, MSAA recreation) are renderer-specific or test-oriented; direct renderer access is not portable.
SetContextRecoveryEnabled(false) lets textures drop CPU shadows; re-enabling cannot rebuild shadows already freed (and on DIRECTX9 the call throws).
concepts.note: DIRECTX9 throw added.

concepts.text: SetStringMarkerEXT is a no-op on most families, real on Vulkan, OpenGL4, SDL_GPU, WebGPU, Metal and FNA3D, and throws "not yet implemented" on DIRECTX9.

RecreateRendererForMultiSampleCount destroys the renderer without preserving resources, state, events or rollback; its header rationale is stale now that Reset applies MSAA; keep it for resource-free tests.
Some CNA-shaped declarations lack a CNAEXT tag (for example the typed user-primitive overload sets), so a strict-surface build proves only that tagged declarations are extensions.

Two VertexPositionColor triangles drawn through BasicEffect with vertex colours and DrawPrimitives; depth occlusion depends on the back buffer having a depth plane (GraphicsDeviceManager default Depth24).
concepts.note: Recreated with the XNA-shaped VertexBuffer constructor and a pass Apply.

concepts.text: The Bible example sources and its screenshot are Bible tooling (tools/cna-screenshot-infra) at an older revision; the screenshot established CPU rasterisation, depth occlusion and interpolation only for that configuration.
concepts.note: The demo sources live in the Bible repository, not in CNA; the page example was re-verified by syntax check only and the screenshot is not reused.

concepts.text: GraphicsDevice is a coherent public state machine, not one uniform native implementation: the shared validation and binding rules are the strongest portable assumptions; presentation, advanced draws, targets and readback need the family's own evidence.
Applied values and discriminating output are more informative than stored requests or property round trips.

Pre-fix Software screenshot from an older revision (white inset where the target should appear); not a TARGET result. The defect and its registered test are described in text instead; the image is not reused.
Software screenshot produced by Bible tooling at an older revision; the example is recreated and syntax-checked, not re-rendered, so no image is published.

issues.text: GraphicsDeviceManager subscribes a raw-this lambda to GameWindow::ClientSizeChanged and never removes it.
GraphicsDeviceManager::Dispose raises Disposed before setting disposed_, so a re-entrant Disposed handler re-runs Dispose.
A PreparingDeviceSettings handler that clears the adapter causes a null dereference in applyToExistingRenderer; a nested ApplyChanges recurses.
Reset rollback covers only window and virtual resolution; failures in the format/MSAA/interval hooks leave partial state and no DeviceReset.
DIRECTX9 throws "not yet implemented" for SetContextRecoveryEnabled and SetStringMarkerEXT.
Construction leak and unconditional video quit, bound-target throw and re-entrant Disposing during device disposal, and GetBackBufferData argument gaps are absent at TARGET.
